chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ الرَّازِي، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَال، عَنِ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ الْجَمَّالِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal who said:

chunks.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ فَقَالَ لِي: يَا صَفْوَانُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنْكَ حَسَنٌ جَمِيلٌ مَا خِلَا شَيْئًا وَاحِدًا قُلْتُ: جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ؟ قَالَ: إِكْرَاؤُكَ جَمَالَكَ مِنْ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ يَعْنِي هَارُونَ قُلْتُ: وَاللَّهَ مَا أَكْرَيْتُهُ أَشَرًا وَلَا بَطَرًا وَلَا لَصَيْدٍ وَلَا لِلهَوِ، وَلَكِنِّي أَكْرِيهِ لِهَذَا الطَّرِيقِ يَعْنِي طَرِيقَ مَكَّةَ، وَلَا أَتَوَلَّاهُ بِنَفْسِي وَلَكِنْ أَنْصِبُ مَعَهُ غِلْمَانِي، فَقَالَ لِي: يَا صَفْوَانُ أَيَقَعُ إِكْرَاؤُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ؟ قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ لِي: أَتُحِبُّ بَقَاءَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ إِكْرَاؤُكَ؟ قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: فَمَنْ أَحَبَّ بَقَاءَهُمْ فَهُوَ مِنْهُمْ وَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْهُمْ كَانَ وَرْدَ النَّارِ، قَالَ صَفْوَانُ: فَذَهَبْتُ وَبَعْتُ جَمَالِي عَنْ آخِرِهَا، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ إِلَى هَارُونَ، فَدَعَانِي فَقَالَ لِي: يَا صَفْوَانُ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّكَ بَعَثْتَ جَمَالَكَ قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، فَقَالَ: لِمَ؟ قُلْتُ: أَنَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ وَالْغِلْمَانُ لَا يَفُونَ بِالْأَعْمَالِ فَقَالَ: هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ إِنِّي لَأَعْلَمُ مَنْ أَشَارَ عَلَيْكَ بِهَذَا أَشَارَ عَلَيْكَ بِهِ مُوسَى بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ! قُلْتُ: مَا لِي وَلِمُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ؟ فَقَالَ: دَعْ هَذَا عَنْكَ فَوَاللَّهَ لَوْلَا حُسْنُ صُحْبَتِكَ لَقَتَلْتُكَ!

translations.en: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) and he said to me: 'O Safwan, everything from you is good and beautiful except for one thing.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, what is that thing?' He said: 'Your renting out your camels to this man,' meaning Harun. I said: 'By Allah, I did not rent them to him out of arrogance or haughtiness, nor for hunting or amusement, but I rent them to him for this path,' meaning the road to Mecca. 'And I do not attend to him personally, but I station my servants with him.' He said to me: 'O Safwan, does the payment of your rent accrue on them?' I said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' He said: 'Do you wish for their survival until your rent is paid?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'So whoever desires their survival is one of them, and whoever is with them will be a resident of the Hellfire.' Safwan said: 'So I went and sold all my camels, every last one of them.' This reached Harun, so he called me and said to me: 'O Safwan, I have heard that you sold your camels.' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Why?' I said: 'I am an old man and the servants are not sufficient for the work.' He said: 'Far off, far off! I know the one who advised you to do this; it is Musa ibn Ja'far who advised you to do this!' I said: 'What do I have to do with Musa ibn Ja'far?' He said: 'Leave that aside, for by Allah, if it were not for your good companionship, I would have killed you!'

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Ikhtiyar* highlights the principle of *al-walā’ wa al-barā’* (loyalty and disavowal) by linking the physical act of renting to the Caliph with spiritual complicity in his eventual fate. The Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that desiring the Caliph's continued rule implies sharing in his accountability, leading Safwan to sell his camels to sever this tie. Harun al-Rashid’s recognition of Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) as the source underscores the growing political and spiritual influence of the Imams during the Abbasid era.
en.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq advise Safwan to stop renting camels to Harun al-Rashid?

key_terms.إِكْرَاء: Renting or leasing (specifically of animals for transport)
key_terms.طَرِيقَ مَكَّةَ: The road to Mecca (referring to the Hajj route)
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنُ جَعَفَرٍ: Musa ibn Ja'far (Imam al-Kazim), the sixth Imam
